scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning:
Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

So, there's an 18-year-old guy who has a 7-year-old brother. The brother is sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he doesn't get enough sleep, he gets all out of sorts the next day. The older brother's friends think the younger brother is really cool and always want to hang out with them. The friends don't have little siblings, so they find him cute and hype him up a lot.

Last night, the mom left the older brother in charge because she wasn't going to be home until 1 AM. She trusted him and his friend, so she said it was fine if the friend came over. The older brother made sure his younger brother went to bed on time because the younger brother can put himself to bed. Then, the friend came over, and they started goofing around, watching a movie, and being kind of loud. This woke up the younger brother, who came downstairs wanting to watch the movie with them.

The older brother told him to go back to bed, but the friend said they should let him stay. The friend started getting the younger brother riled up, and the older brother knew that if he tried to force him to go to bed, he'd have to drag him upstairs, which would be embarrassing and exhausting. So, he let the younger brother sit on the couch with them. By the time the movie ended, the friend had to go home, and the younger brother was basically asleep. The older brother carried him upstairs around midnight and put him in bed.

The next morning, the younger brother didn't want to get up, even though on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past 8 AM. He was pretty cranky. The mom found out that the older brother let him stay up late and got mad at him. The older brother thinks that since the younger brother is 7, he should know about consequences and that if he stays up later, he won't feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. He also told his mom that two hours of missed sleep for a kid his age wasn't a big deal. Now, he's wondering if he's AITA (Ask if I'm the Asshole) for not forcing his brother to go to bed.

Alright, so the question is whether the older brother's action of not forcing his younger brother to go to bed is morally acceptable or not. If it's acceptable, the answer is 1; if not, it's 0.

First, I need to understand the context better. The older brother is 18, and the younger is 7. The younger brother is sensitive to sleep deprivation, meaning that not getting enough sleep affects his behavior the next day. The older brother's friends find the younger brother cute and hype him up, which probably makes the younger brother more excited and less likely to go to bed when he should.

The older brother was in charge because the mom wasn't home until 1 AM. He made sure the younger brother went to bed on time, which is good. Then, the friend came over, and they started being loud, which woke up the younger brother. The older brother told him to go back to bed, but the friend encouraged him to stay. The older brother was in a tough spot because if he tried to force the younger brother to go to bed, it would lead to a tantrum, which would be embarrassing and exhausting.

So, he let the younger brother stay, and by the end of the movie, the younger brother was asleep. The older brother carried him upstairs and put him to bed around midnight. The next day, the younger brother was cranky and slept in, which the mom noticed and got mad at the older brother.

The older brother's reasoning is that the younger brother should know about consequences and that staying up late would make him feel bad. He also thinks that two hours of missed sleep isn't a big deal for a 7-year-old.

Now, I need to evaluate whether the older brother's action was morally acceptable or not.

First, let's consider the responsibility aspect. The older brother was in charge of his younger brother, so he had a duty to ensure that the younger brother got enough sleep. The younger brother is 7, which is young enough that he might not fully understand the consequences of staying up late, even though the older brother thinks he should.

The older brother made sure the younger brother went to bed on time initially, which is responsible. However, when the younger brother was woken up by the noise, the older brother had to decide whether to enforce bedtime or let him stay up. He chose to let him stay up because he didn't want to deal with the tantrum and the potential embarrassment.

This decision could be seen as prioritizing his own comfort and convenience over his brother's well-being. By letting the younger brother stay up, he knew that the younger brother would likely be cranky the next day, which did happen. The mom got mad because she knew the older brother had let him stay up late.

On the other hand, the older brother might argue that he was trying to avoid a difficult situation and that two hours of missed sleep isn't a significant amount for a 7-year-old. He also believes that the younger brother should learn about consequences, which is a valid point.

However, the younger brother is only 7, and while he might understand the concept of consequences to some extent, he might not fully grasp the impact of staying up late on his mood and behavior. The older brother's approach of letting him stay up and then dealing with the consequences the next day might not be the most effective way to teach responsibility, especially given the younger brother's sensitivity to sleep deprivation.

Additionally, the older brother's decision to let the younger brother stay up could be seen as neglecting his responsibility to ensure his brother's well-being. By allowing the younger brother to stay up, he was putting him in a situation where he would likely feel unwell the next day, which could have been avoided if he had enforced bedtime.

Moreover, the older brother's reasoning that two hours of missed sleep isn't a big deal might not take into account the individual sensitivity of the younger brother. While two hours might not seem like a lot, for someone who is particularly sensitive to sleep deprivation, it could have a noticeable impact on their behavior and mood.

In terms of the older brother's own feelings, he was trying to avoid a tantrum and potential embarrassment, which are valid concerns. However, as the responsible adult in charge, his priority should be the well-being of his younger brother, even if it means dealing with a difficult situation in the moment.

Furthermore, the older brother's decision to let the younger brother stay up could set a precedent for future behavior. If the younger brother learns that he can stay up late by causing a scene, he might try to do it again, leading to more instances of sleep deprivation and crankiness.

In conclusion, while the older brother's intentions might have been to avoid immediate conflict and embarrassment, his decision to let the younger brother stay up late, knowing the potential negative consequences, could be seen as morally unacceptable because it prioritized his own convenience over his brother's well-being and failed to fulfill his responsibility to ensure his brother's adequate rest.
